::: {.why}
You cannot use one convention for both, and the day you forget that is the day a portfolio return is silently wrong by an amount too small to notice and too large to ignore.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Give the one line of algebra showing that log returns aggregate over time, and the one line showing simple returns aggregate over assets.
- Say what goes wrong, numerically, if you build a portfolio by weighting log returns.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Do both derivations on paper, in four lines total. Time aggregation is the telescoping product of gross returns. Cross-sectional aggregation is the weighted sum of gross returns minus one. Then say why no convention aggregates in both directions.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Measure the error you would have made: build your ten-name equal-weighted portfolio the wrong way, by averaging log returns, and compare its cumulative path to the correct construction over ten years. Report the terminal gap in percent. It will be small enough to have gone unnoticed and large enough to matter.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the convention into qlib/ as a docstring rule at the top of a new returns module: prices to log returns for anything through time, gross simple returns for anything across names. You will read that docstring in week 24.
:::
:::

::: {.checkpoint}

:::
